chapter: Ray Charles and the shelved album
title: Lubinsky blocks the album
summary: Lubinsky threatened Ray, who shelved the record to protect himself.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: When did you first learn that there was trouble with the album from a legal point of view?

He told Ray – he even threatened the boy. He said, “I’ll have you put in jail for life.” He said, “Because that’s my artist that you recorded.” He kept threatening, calling him, threatening him. So of course, I didn’t feel bad when Ray stopped the record. He stopped the record to protect hisself. I can understand that, and I took it like that, that Ray stopped the record and put it on the shelf until he could get a clearance.
But the other thing that always blows my mind about this story is that – so you’re in L.A., and it looks like you’ll be in L.A. to stay, because you really like L.A. . . .
. . . and there’s more opportunities there for show business and . . .
